title: group_oscore: _previous retains every historical key forever (forward-secrecy gap)
description: python/src/lichen/crypto/group_oscore.py:122,195,164-171: rekey() appends to _previous and nothing purges it; key_valid_at only gates use past the grace window while the material stays in memory (and key_for_epoch does a growing linear scan). A single memory compromise of the controller retroactively exposes all past group traffic keys, contradicting the module's forward-secrecy framing and the docstring's 'previous epoch+key' (singular) design. Fix: after rekey, drop entries whose created_s + GRACE_PERIOD_S < now and zeroize where practical.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2f2010b3f0: rekey now purges _previous entries with created_s + GRACE_PERIOD_S < now (strict boundary consistent with key_valid_at), so superseded key material is no longer retained indefinitely; dropped bytearray key buffers are zeroized in place (bytes documented as unscrubbable), including collision-dropped wrap entries. GroupKeyMaterial.key widened to bytes|bytearray for the zeroization path. Test: TestPreviousRetention pins that after grace elapses on the injected clock _previous no longer holds the old material (key_for_epoch(1) is None) and that a dropped bytearray key is overwritten with zeros. Suite: 19 passed in python/tests/crypto/test_group_oscore.py; ruff clean.
